references.cited_as: Bhatia A, et al. PLoS Med. 2025;22(1):e1004493
references.record_title: Effect of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) on hospitalization among adults with COVID-19: An electronic health record-based target trial emulation from N3C.
references.notes: Printed title, authors and pages corrected (was a paraphrased title with no authors). Absolute risk reductions added beside the relative figures. Publication date 2025-01-17 per PubMed record supports "January 2025". Citable summary link previously pointed to an unrelated TB trial (10.1371/journal.pmed.1004393, labelled "Xie et al."); now links this record.

claims.text: 703,647 patients at 34 US sites, April 2022 to August 2023
claims.quote: a cohort of 703,647 patients with COVID-19 seen at 34 clinical sites across the United States between April 1, 2022 and August 28, 2023

claims.text: 39% reduction in hospitalization (95% CI 36% to 41%, P<0.001), absolute 0.9 percentage points
claims.quote: Paxlovid reduced the risk of hospitalization by 39% (95% confidence interval (CI) [36%, 41%]; p < 0.001), with an absolute risk reduction of 0.9 percentage points

claims.text: 61% reduction in death (95% CI 55% to 67%, P<0.001), absolute 0.2 percentage points
claims.quote: reduced the risk of death by 61% (95% CI [55%, 67%]; p < 0.001), with an absolute risk reduction of 0.2 percentage points

claims.text: Absolute hospitalization reduction similar in vaccinated and unvaccinated, much greater in 65+ (also supports "Age 65 or older" benefit item)
claims.quote: Absolute risk reduction for hospitalization was similar among patients that were vaccinated and unvaccinate, but was much greater among patients aged 65+ years than among younger patients.

claims.text: Effective including in vaccinated patients, in the Omicron era (Key Takeaway, summary, Bottom Line)
claims.quote: Paxlovid is effective at preventing hospitalization and death, including among vaccinated patients, and particularly among older patients. This remains true in the era of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Omicron subvariants.

claims.text: Millions of courses prescribed in the United States alone
claims.quote: Millions of treatment courses have been prescribed in the United States alone.

claims.text: EPIC-SR population: fully vaccinated with at least one risk factor, plus unvaccinated (or not vaccinated within a year) without risk factors
claims.quote: Patients who were fully vaccinated against Covid-19 and who had at least one risk factor for severe disease, as well as patients without such risk factors who had never been vaccinated

claims.text: No significant difference in time to sustained symptom alleviation, 12 vs 13 days, P=0.60
claims.quote: The median time to sustained alleviation of all targeted signs and symptoms of Covid-19 was 12 days in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group and 13 days in the placebo group (P = 0.60).

claims.text: Hospitalization or death 0.8% vs 1.6%, difference not statistically significant (95% CI -2.0 to 0.4)
claims.quote: Five participants (0.8%) in the nirmatrelvir-ritonavir group and 10 (1.6%) in the placebo group were hospitalized for Covid-19 or died from any cause (difference, -0.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.0 to 0.4).

references.record_title: SARS-CoV-2 Virologic Rebound With Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir Therapy : An Observational Study.
references.notes: New ref 3, the primary paper behind the former Harvard Medical School news item. The news item said 142 participants; the paper analysed 72 treated and 55 untreated (127). Shedding was median 14 vs 3 days (not "fewer than 5"). Scite flags one contrasting citation (10.1002/jmv.29333: higher clinical rebound than previously reported); it does not change the cited claims.

claims.text: Boston observational cohort, 72 treated vs 55 untreated
claims.quote: Compared with untreated persons (= 55), those taking N-R (= 72) were older, received more COVID-19 vaccinations, and more commonly had immunosuppression.

claims.text: Virologic rebound 20.8% vs 1.8%; about 1 in 5
claims.quote: Fifteen participants (20.8%) taking N-R had VR versus 1 (1.8%) who was untreated

claims.text: Positive culture after prior negative; shedding median 14 vs 3 days; live virus shed during rebound
claims.quote: All persons with VR had a positive viral culture result after a prior negative result. ... those who had VR had prolonged shedding of replication-competent virus compared with those who did not have VR (median, 14 vs. 3 days).

claims.text: Half with virologic rebound reported symptom rebound
claims.quote: Eight of 16 participants (50% [CI, 25% to 75%]) with VR also reported symptom rebound

claims.text: About 1 in 5 (summary, Key Takeaway)
claims.quote: Virologic rebound occurred in approximately 1 in 5 people taking N-R, often without symptom rebound, and was associated with shedding of replication-competent virus.
